evals.name: boot4-maven-with-tests
evals.prompt: Add a Dapr workflow to the Spring Boot app in ./claims-api. When a claim is submitted it should verify the policy, assess the damage and then pay out the claim, one after the other. Show me your plan first, then go ahead without waiting for my approval.
evals.expected_output: A plan, then targeted edits to claims-api: the dapr-spring-bom 1.19.1 import and dapr-spring-boot-starter in pom.xml, @EnableDaprWorkflows on ClaimsApplication, a chained workflow with three top-level @Component activities and records, a controller under /workflows/<route> whose start answers 409 for an active instance, POST /claims also starting the workflow (default yes), dapr.yaml with appPort 8082 (read from server.port) and resources/statestore.yaml, a workflow.http file, DAPR-WORKFLOW.md; `mvn -q -DskipTests package` succeeds and `mvn -q test` passes all three existing tests; README untouched.
expectations: Before the first file change, the response (or transcript) contains an Add Workflow Plan that names the target claims-api, Spring Boot 4.0.8 with Maven, server.port 8082 as the app port, and lists every file it will add or edit; its Questions section asks whether `POST /claims` should also start the workflow, with yes as the default, and asks no dependency-update question (the project has no Dapr dependency yet)

pom.xml imports io.dapr.spring dapr-spring-bom 1.19.1 (type pom, scope import) in dependencyManagement and adds dapr-spring-boot-starter without a <version>; the parent stays spring-boot-starter-parent 4.0.8, java.version stays 17, and the existing spring-boot-starter-webmvc and spring-boot-starter-test dependencies are unchanged
ClaimsApplication.java carries exactly one @EnableDaprWorkflows next to @SpringBootApplication, and no second @SpringBootApplication class exists

A top-level @Component workflow class implementing io.dapr.workflows.Workflow calls three activities in sequence (verify policy, assess damage, pay out) with ctx.callActivity(<Activity>.class.getName(), ..., <Output>.class).await(); each activity is a top-level @Component implementing WorkflowActivity; every payload is a top-level record; the workflow contains no Instant.now(), UUID.randomUUID(), Thread, CompletableFuture or catch (Exception

A new @RestController with @RequestMapping("/workflows/<route>") takes DaprWorkflowClient through its constructor into a final field and has start, status, pause, resume and terminate handlers; start answers 409 Conflict when getWorkflowState shows the instance RUNNING, PENDING, SUSPENDED or CONTINUED_AS_NEW (after the exists check), and status uses getWorkflowState with the exists(...) check; no getInstanceState, waitForInstanceCompletion, purgeInstance or field @Autowired anywhere

ClaimController's POST handler still calls claims.submit(claim) and returns ResponseEntity.created(...) with the same body, and (the default yes) now also calls workflowClient.scheduleNewWorkflow for the workflow with the submitted claim's id as instance id after submit succeeds; DaprWorkflowClient is a constructor parameter and final field; the GET handler is unchanged

dapr.yaml is created in the claims-api folder with one app entry whose appPort is 8082 and whose command is ["mvn", "spring-boot:run"], and resources/statestore.yaml has actorStateStore "true"; application.properties is byte-for-byte unchanged (server.port 8082 stays)

README.md is byte-for-byte unchanged and DAPR-WORKFLOW.md exists in claims-api with how to start (`dapr run -f .`), request examples on port 8082 under /workflows/<route>, and a Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard section with the macOS/Linux and Windows install commands

The transcript shows `mvn -q -DskipTests package` after the code steps and a final `mvn -q test` that passes (ClaimServiceTest's two tests and ClaimsApplicationTests.contextLoads, 3 tests, 0 failures) without a running Dapr sidecar
No files outside the plan were changed: ClaimService.java, Claim.java and everything under src/test are unchanged
No git command other than `git status` was run

Dev Dashboard: before changing files the agent runs `diagrid-dev-dashboard --version` once without stopping, and the final output ends with exactly `Dapr Workflow is added to claims-api. Open DAPR-WORKFLOW.md in the claims-api folder for what changed and how to run it.` followed only by the matching Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard recommendation

evals.name: existing-dapr-older-pin
evals.prompt: In ./returns-platform/returns-service, add a Dapr workflow for product returns: when started for a return it waits up to 14 days for a ParcelReceived event, then inspects the parcel and refunds the customer; if the parcel never arrives it closes the return. Show the plan, then proceed without asking me.
evals.expected_output: The plan offers the dependency update (dapr-spring-bom 1.18.1 → 1.19.1, dapr-spring-boot-4-starter → dapr-spring-boot-starter, default yes), asks about POST /returns with default no and a Risk line because ReturnControllerTest calls it through MockMvc, reads server.port 8090 from application.yml and flags the collision with label-printer in dapr.yaml, reuses returns-store, appends an app entry to the parent dapr.yaml, puts @EnableDaprWorkflows on a separate @Configuration class because of the @WebMvcTest slice test, and adds an external-event workflow with a raise-event endpoint. Build and both existing tests pass.
expectations: Before the first file change the plan says a newer Dapr version is available (dapr-spring-bom 1.18.1 → 1.19.1, with dapr-spring-boot-4-starter replaced by dapr-spring-boot-starter because 1.19 has no separate Boot 4 starter) and asks whether to update, with yes as the default; with that default, pom.xml imports dapr-spring-bom 1.19.1 and depends on dapr-spring-boot-starter without a <version>, no dapr-spring-boot-4-starter remains, and the parent stays at 4.0.5

Before the first file change the plan asks whether `POST /returns` should also start the workflow with **no** as the default, and has a Risk line saying ReturnControllerTest calls that endpoint through MockMvc and would need a running sidecar or a mocked DaprWorkflowClient; with that default ReturnController.java is byte-for-byte unchanged

The plan names app port 8090, read from server.port in src/main/resources/application.yml, and flags that label-printer already uses appPort 8090 in ../dapr.yaml; application.yml is byte-for-byte unchanged
No new component with actorStateStore "true" is created: components/statestore.yaml is unchanged, no resources/ folder is created, and the plan says the existing returns-store is reused

returns-platform/dapr.yaml keeps resourcesPath ./components and the label-printer entry unchanged, and gains one returns-service entry with appDirPath returns-service, appPort 8090, a daprHTTPPort other than 3510 and command ["mvn", "spring-boot:run"]; no dapr.yaml is created inside returns-service

The workflow waits with ctx.waitForExternalEvent(..., Duration.ofDays(14), <record>.class).await() inside try/catch (TaskCanceledException e) and completes with a closed or timed-out result in the catch; it catches no Exception or Throwable

The new workflow controller under /workflows/<route> has a raise-event handler that binds the body as Object and checks the instance with getWorkflowState and exists(...) before raiseEvent, and its start handler answers 409 for an active instance

Because ReturnControllerTest is a @WebMvcTest slice test, ReturnsApplication.java is byte-for-byte unchanged and @EnableDaprWorkflows sits once on a new @Configuration class in com.example.returns (for example DaprWorkflowConfiguration); the plan says why
The transcript shows a successful `mvn -q -DskipTests package` and a final `mvn -q test` with ReturnControllerTest's 2 tests passing
No git command other than `git status` was run

evals.name: bare-webmvctest-risk
evals.prompt: Add a Dapr workflow to the Spring Boot app in ./invoices-api: when an invoice is issued it should validate the invoice and then send it to the customer, one after the other.
evals.expected_output: An Add Workflow Plan and a request for approval; no file in invoices-api is changed. Because InvoiceControllerTest is a bare @WebMvcTest (no controllers listed), the plan puts @EnableDaprWorkflows on a new DaprWorkflowConfiguration class and carries a Risk line: the test also loads the new workflow controller and fails without a DaprWorkflowClient bean, so it needs a @MockitoBean DaprWorkflowClient field or its controllers listed; the skill does not edit tests. The test does not call POST /invoices, so the endpoint question keeps its default yes.
expectations: The response contains an Add Workflow Plan naming the target invoices-api, Spring Boot 4.0.8 with Maven, and app port 8084 read from server.port in application.properties, and ends by asking the user to approve, change or stop

The plan has a Risk line that names InvoiceControllerTest as a @WebMvcTest without listed controllers, says it will also load the new workflow controller and fail because no DaprWorkflowClient bean exists in the slice, and names the fix (a @MockitoBean DaprWorkflowClient field, or listing the controllers as in @WebMvcTest(InvoiceController.class)) without planning to edit the test
The plan puts @EnableDaprWorkflows on a new @Configuration class (for example DaprWorkflowConfiguration) because of the slice test, and lists InvoicesApplication.java as unchanged or not edited

The Questions section asks whether `POST /invoices` should also start the workflow with yes as the default (no test calls that endpoint), and asks no dependency-update question (the project has no Dapr dependency)
No file in the invoices-api fixture is added, changed or deleted (hash check), and no `mvn` command or file write was run on the fixture
